content: 1. Ethinyl estradiol, when co-administered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and/or dasabuvir, can lead to significant toxicity due to an unspecified interaction mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. Clinical trials have shown ALT elevations greater than 5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), with some cases exceeding 20 times ULN. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued prior to initiating therapy with these hepatitis C combination drugs and can be restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 2. Otesaconazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates, including ethinyl estradiol. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. The lowest starting dose of the BCRP substrate should be used, or its dose should be reduced. 3. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 4. Paromomycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Penicillin G and Penicillin VK decrease ethinyl estradiol levels by increasing its metabolism or altering intestinal flora, respectively. These interactions may lead to oral contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Pentobarbital and phenobarbital reduce the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may become unreliable, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are advised. 7. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable when co-administered, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 8. Pioglitazone decreases ethinyl estradiol levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Posaconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable when co-administered, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 11. Quinidine increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative drugs or close monitoring are advised. 12. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Ethinyl estradiol increases ramelteon levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Ranolazine levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternative drugs or close monitoring are recommended. 15. Rasagiline levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Repotrectinib decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may become ineffective, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 17. Ribociclib increases ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Rifabutin, rifampin, and rifapentine decrease ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable when co-administered, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 19. Ritonavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 20. Romidepsin decreases ethinyl estradiol effects through receptor binding competition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Ropinirole levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Rosuvastatin increases ethinyl estradiol levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Rucaparib increases ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Rufinamide decreases ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 25. Ruxolitinib levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Selegiline levels are increased by oral contraceptives through inhibition of N-demethylation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 27. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, potentially altering the metabolism of CYP substrates. Caution is advised when co-administered with drugs that have a narrow therapeutic index. 28. Somapacitan, somatrogon, and somatropin levels are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Higher doses of growth hormone analogs may be required. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 29. St. John’s Wort decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives may become ineffective, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 30. Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer, potentially altering the effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Sugammadex decreases ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone effects through receptor binding competition. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended for seven days following administration. 32. Sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, and sulfisoxazole decrease ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Tacrolimus levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are recommended.
